newsitem.title: USA: Colo. police want to talk to slain girl's parents.
newsitem.headline: Colo. police want to talk to slain girl's parents.

text.p: Police investigating the murder of 6-year-old JonBenet Ramsey on Tuesday offered little new information on the case, saying they still hope to set up a formal interview with the girl's parents.
"The Ramseys are not under arrest," Leslie Aaholm, Boulder police spokeswoman said.
John and Patricia Ramsey, in an interview with CNN, denied any involvement in their daughter's murder. But both have hired attorneys and have yet to be interviewed formally by Boulder police.

The little girl's body was found on Dec. 26 in the basement of the family's 15-room home about eight hours after her mother said she had found a ransom note demanding $118,000 on the back staircase of the Boulder residence.

Aaholm said police were still trying to work out the scheduling for an interview. In a briefing, she said police have not ruled out the kidnapping aspect of the case, but have been focusing on the murder of the child beauty pageant winner.
Aaholm said an older half-brother, John, 20, had given blood, hair and handwriting samples but could not say if he had been formally interviewed by police.

However, he and his sister Melinda, John Ramsey's children from a former marriage, were out of town at the time of the murder. Other family members including the parents have given police similar samples.
Aaholm shed little light on information police may have obtained through a search of the family's other home in Michigan.

The blond, blue-eyed JonBenet was strangled. According to news reports her skull was fractured and she was sexually assaulted. She had been crowned Little Miss Colorado and participated in other beauty contests.
